questions.q: If the collision frequency of hydrogen molecules in a closed chamber at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is $\mathrm{Z}$, then the collision frequency of the same system at $127^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assuming mean free path constant.
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{f} \propto \mathrm{V} \propto \sqrt{\mathrm{T}} \\ & \frac{\mathrm{f}_1}{\mathrm{f}_2}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}_1}{\mathrm{~T}_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{300}{400}} \\ & \mathrm{f}_2=\sqrt{\frac{4}{3}}=\mathrm{f}_1=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \mathrm{Z}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The mean free path and the average speed of oxygen molecules at 300 K and 1 atm are $3 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~m}$ and $600 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ respectively. Find the frequency of its collisions.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Frequency }=\frac{1}{T}=\frac{V_{\text {avg }}}{\lambda} \\ & =\frac{600}{3 \times 157}=2 \times 10^9 \mathrm{sec}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The temperature at which the kinetic energy of oxygen molecules becomes double than its value at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy is given by KE=f2kT.

Let the kinetic energy be K1 at 27 °C and the kinetic energy be K' at T' temperature. As given in the question, K'=2K1. Hence, 

K'K1=T'T⇒2=T'300⇒T'=600 K

In Celsius the temperature is T'-273=327 °C.

questions.q: The number density of molecules of a gas depends on their distance r from the origin as, <math><mi>n</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>α</mi><msup><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> Then the numer of molecules is proportional to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Density of molecules of gas as a of r is, n(r)=n0e-αr4
Total no. of molecules =∫0∞n(r)dv
∫0∞n0 e-αr44πr2 dr
To integrate this, substitute u=α3/4r3  this will give us dr=13α3/4r2du
Now, the integration will become, 4πn03α3/4 ∫0∞ e-u4/3du
This shows that the numer of molecules is proportional to n0α-3/4

questions.q: What will be the average value of energy along one degree of freedom for an ideal gas in thermal equilibrium at a temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo> </mo><mo>?</mo></math> (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> is Boltzmann constant)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy associated with each degree of freedom per molecule =12kBT.

Hence, the average value of energy along one degree of freedom for an ideal gas in thermal equilibrium at a temperature T =12kBT.

questions.q: The number of air molecules per cm3 is increased from 3×1019 to 12×1019. The ratio of collision frequency of air molecules before and after the increase in number respectively is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is 

n1=3×1019n2=12×1019

The mean time between two collision has the meaning of a period τ, since it indicates the repetitive time intervals in which on average collisions take place. The reciprocal of the time τ can be understood as the collision frequency f, which indicates the number of collisions per unit time.The collision frequency is also directly proportional to the number molecules per unit volume.

f∝1τ

⇒f∝n

⇒f1 f2 =n1n2=3×101912×1019=0.25

questions.q: When a gas filled in a closed vessel is heated by raising the temperature by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>, its pressure increases by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo></math> The initial temperature of the gas is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics

From ideal gas equation, PV=nRT, where, n is amount of substance, R is ideal gas constant and V is volume.

In closed vessel volume remains constant.

So, dPP×100=dTT×100

0.4=1T×100

⇒T=250 K

questions.q: $\gamma_{\mathrm{A}}$ is the specific heat ratio of monoatomic gas A having 3 translational degrees of freedom. $\gamma_B$ is the specific heat ratio of polyatomic gas B having 3 translational, 3 rotational degrees of freedom and 1 vibrational mode. If $\frac{\gamma_{\mathrm{A}}}{\gamma_{\mathrm{B}}}=\left(1+\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}\right)$, then the value of $n$ is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\gamma_A}{\gamma_B}=\frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}+2}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{A}}} \times \frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{B}}+2} \\ & =\frac{3+2}{3} \times \frac{(6+2)}{(6+2)+2} \\ & =\frac{5}{3} \times \frac{8}{10}=\frac{40}{30} \\ & \because \frac{40}{30}=1+\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{40}{30}-1=\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}\end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=3$

questions.q: One mole of a monoatomic gas is mixed with three moles of a diatomic gas. The molecular specific heat of mixture at constant volume is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msup><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mi>R</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>; then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> will be _____ . (Assume that the given diatomic gas has no vibrational mode.)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Molecular specific heat at constant volume in terms of degrees of freedom is given by CV=f2R

Molecular specific heat of mixture at constant volume is CV/mix=n1CV1+n2CV2n1+n2

=1×3R2+3×5R21+3

=9R4=α24R

⇒α=3
